mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) in periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4.0% for two consecutive months indicates an overheating labor market, which historically precedes slower earnings growth and higher input costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE < 4.0% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during periods of two consecutive quarterly GDPC1 declines.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals supply-side stress, which raises input costs and dampens profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during three consecutive months of INDPRO below its 12-month MA.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month averages signals a monetary policy tightening coinciding with rising inflation, which historically has been associated with negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to higher discount rates and margin compression.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A strong month-over-month increase in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) combined with a simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) signals a divergence between income growth and capital spending, which historically precedes equity market corrections over the next 60 trading days due to misallocation and delayed investment.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 0.5% MoM AND HOUST < previous month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS rises >0.5% MoM and HOUST falls month-on-month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 6.0% for three consecutive months signals a deepening labor market weakness, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of monetary policy stance.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during three consecutive months of UNRATE > 6.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which typically boosts corporate earnings and supports higher equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive during four consecutive months of RSAFS above its 12-month moving average.
